{{Short description|On a property of surjective continuous maps between compact metric spaces}}
{{distinguish|Morse–Sard–Federer theorem}}

{{context|date=March 2017}}
In mathematics, the '''Federer–Morse theorem''', introduced by {{harvs|txt|author2-link=Anthony Morse|last2=Morse|author1-link=Herbert Federer|last1=Federer|year=1943}},  states that if ''f'' is a [[surjective function|surjective]] [[continuous map]] from a [[Compact_space#Metric_spaces|compact metric space]] ''X'' to a compact metric space ''Y'', then there is a [[Borel subset]] ''Z'' of ''X'' such that ''f'' restricted to ''Z'' is a [[bijection]] from ''Z'' to ''Y''.<ref>Section 4 of {{harvs|txt|last=Parthasarathy|year=1967}}.</ref>
Moreover, the inverse of that restriction is a Borel [[Section_(category_theory)|section]] of ''f''—it is a [[Borel isomorphism]].<ref>Page 12 of {{harvs|txt|last=Fabec|year=2000}}</ref>
